mainTopic: שינוי בעלים in a פסח during the year, and the new משנה on slaughtering the פסח for improper eaters and at improper times
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rejection of רב פפא's attempt to learn the law of שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש. The גמרא lists four ways שינוי קודש is a stronger disqualification. It then admits that two of the four differences can be challenged, but insists that the other two still hold. רבא gives a new reason instead: a פסח slaughtered during the year with שינוי בעלים is treated as if it had no owner at its proper time, so it is פסול. A new משנה then teaches that a פסח slaughtered only for people who cannot eat it or are not registered for it is פסול, while a mixed intention leaves it כשר. The same משנה sets the time rules: before חצות it is פסול, and before the תמיד it is כשר. The גמרא defines 'not its eaters' and 'not its members' and finds their sources in the verse. במכסת and תכוסו make registration לעכב, רבי reads תכוסו as 'slaughter', and a היקש links eaters to members.

steps.title: Finishing the list of differences between the two disqualifications
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its rejection of רב פפא's comparison. שינוי קודש applies after death and to communal offerings. שינוי בעלים has neither of these features and lacks the other two as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, a change of sanctity applies after the owner's death, and it applies to communal offerings the same as to an individual's offering. Can you say the same about a change of owner? Its disqualification is not in the animal itself, it does not apply to all four services, it does not apply after death, and it does not apply to communal offerings the same as to an individual's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its argument that you cannot learn שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש, because שינוי קודש is a stronger kind of disqualification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has four points. שינוי קודש is a flaw in the animal itself, works in all four עבודות, applies after the owner dies, and applies to a קרבן ציבור. שינוי בעלים fails on all four, so a law about the stronger case cannot simply be carried over to the weaker one.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering an offering with intent that it be a different type of קרבן
Slaughtering an offering with intent that it be for a different owner
Its disqualification is in the animal itself
The four blood services: slaughtering, receiving, carrying, and sprinkling
A communal offering treated the same as an individual's offering

steps.confusionAlert: The first two points (in the animal itself, and the four services) were said on the previous amud. Here the גמרא adds the last two and then lists all four on the שינוי בעלים side.

phrases.english: And it (change of sanctity) applies after death,
and it applies to a communal offering just as to an individual's.
Will you say the same about a change of owner?
phrases.notes: He's asking to make a point: you can't say the same thing here.

phrases.english: For its disqualification is not in the animal itself,
and it does not apply to all four services,
and it does not apply after death,
and it does not apply to a communal offering as to an individual's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the refutation of רב פפא's derivation, which began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the law of שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שינוי קודש is a stronger disqualification in four ways, so it cannot teach about the weaker שינוי בעלים.

steps.title: Two of the differences are shaky, but two are solid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that two of the four differences are not airtight. It insists that the other two are definitely accurate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though two of these differences are not exact, two of them at least are exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to qualify its own list. It is setting up the next steps, which will explain which two differences are weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation does not need all four differences. Even two solid ones are enough to block the comparison, so weakening the other two does not save רב פפא's derivation.

keyTerms.meaning: Not exact; not meant precisely
At least two

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְתֵּי לָאו דַּוְקָא,
phrases.english: And even though two are not exact,
two, at least, are exact.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְתֵּי לָאו דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the four-point list from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the four differences, two can be challenged, but two remain valid.

steps.title: The first weak difference: both are only a matter of thought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that only שינוי קודש is a flaw in the animal itself. Both disqualifications come only from the כהן's wrong intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is different about a change of owner, that its disqualification is not in the animal itself? Is it because its disqualification is merely a thought? A change of sanctity is also merely a disqualification of thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first difference, being a flaw in the animal itself, is not exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שינוי בעלים is called 'not in the animal' because it comes only from intention, then שינוי קודש should be called that too. Both are disqualifications of מחשבה, so this point does not truly separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Merely a thought or intention

phrases.english: For what is different about a change of owner
that its disqualification is not in the animal itself?
Because its disqualification is merely a thought?
A change of sanctity too,
its disqualification is merely a thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two weak differences mentioned in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both disqualifications come from intention alone, so neither one is truly a flaw in the animal's body.

steps.title: The second weak difference: רב פנחס holds it applies after death
steps.stepSummary: The claim that שינוי בעלים does not apply after death is disputed. רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי holds that it does apply after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, about what was said, that a change of owner does not apply after death: according to רב פנחס son of רב אמי, who said that a change of owner does apply after death, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second difference, the one about after death, is not exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This difference only works if everyone agrees that שינוי בעלים stops applying after the owner dies. Since רב פנחס disagrees, the point is not universally true.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
רב פנחס, son of רב אמי, an אמורא
What is there to say? (there is no good answer)

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was said,
that a change of owner does not apply after death:
but according to רב פנחס son of רב אמי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ שִׁינּוּי בְּעָלִים לְאַחַר מִיתָה,
phrases.english: who said a change of owner does apply after death,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second of the two weak differences.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference about applying after death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אמורא explicitly holds that שינוי בעלים applies after death, so this difference is disputed.

steps.title: Two differences still stand
steps.stepSummary: Despite both challenges, the four services and the communal-offering differences remain. Those two are enough to reject the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two of them, at least, are exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the side discussion and repeats that the refutation still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two remaining differences are that only שינוי קודש applies to all four עבודות and to a קרבן ציבור. These are enough to block the comparison, so רב פפא's derivation stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: They are

steps.whatToRemember: Two solid differences (the four services, and communal offerings) are enough to show that שינוי קודש cannot teach about שינוי בעלים.

phrases.english: At least two are exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up after the two challenges in steps 3 and 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The derivation from שינוי קודש remains refuted on the strength of two valid differences.

steps.title: רבא's new reason: treated as having no owner at its proper time
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation. A פסח slaughtered during the year with שינוי בעלים is viewed as if it had no owner at its proper time, and it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: A פסח that one slaughtered during the rest of the year with a change of owner is treated like one that has no owner at its proper time, and it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב פפא's approach and brings רבא's different reason for the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not compare to שינוי קודש. He judges the animal by its own proper time, ערב פסח, when שינוי בעלים would disqualify a פסח. A פסח slaughtered this way is treated as having no real owner, so even during the year it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the previous approach)
The rest of the days of the year
At its proper time (ערב פסח)
Disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: The law is the same as before, but the reason is new. רבא measures the פסח by its proper time, when it would count as having no owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא keeping the הלכה while replacing a failed source with a sounder explanation.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered during the rest of the year
with a change of owner

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בְּעָלִים בִּזְמַנּוֹ,
phrases.english: is treated like one that has no owner at its proper time,
and it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected derivation with a new reason for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered during the year with שינוי בעלים is פסול, because it is treated as lacking an owner at its proper time.

steps.title: Slaughtering the פסח for the wrong people
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a פסח slaughtered only for unfit or unregistered people is פסול. If it is slaughtered for a mix of fit and unfit people, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered the פסח for people who cannot eat it, or for people not signed up for it, or for ערלים or טמאים, it is פסול. If he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and those who cannot, for registered and unregistered people, for circumcised and uncircumcised, or for impure and pure, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists improper intentions about who will eat the פסח and says which ones ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having only unfit eaters in mind makes the פסח פסול. If at least some of the intended eaters are fit, it stays כשר. A partly bad intention does not ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Its eaters: people able to eat the פסח
Its registered members: people who signed up for this animal
Uncircumcised men, who may not eat the פסח
Ritually impure people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. 'Only unfit people' makes it פסול. 'Fit and unfit people together' makes it כשר.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he slaughtered it not for its eaters,
phrases.notes: People who cannot eat even a כזית.

phrases.english: or not for its registered members,
or for the uncircumcised or the impure, it is disqualified.
For its eaters and for those not its eaters,
for its registered members and for those not registered,
for the circumcised and the uncircumcised,
for the impure and the pure, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous sugya about שינוי בעלים ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention for only unfit or unregistered eaters makes the פסח פסול. A mixed intention leaves it כשר.

steps.title: The time limits for slaughtering the פסח
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering before חצות is פסול because of בין הערבים. Slaughtering before the תמיד is כשר, as long as the blood is kept stirred. Even if the פסח's blood is thrown first, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it before midday, it is פסול, because the Torah says 'in the afternoon'. If he slaughtered it before the afternoon תמיד, it is כשר. But someone else should stir its blood until the תמיד's blood is thrown. And if the פסח's blood was thrown first, it is still כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second topic: when the פסח may be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before חצות is not yet בין הערבים, so the פסח is פסול. The correct order is תמיד first and פסח after. Breaking that order does not ruin the פסח, but the blood is stirred so it does not clot while waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Midday
'In the afternoon', the Torah's time for the פסח
The daily communal offering, brought here in the afternoon
Stirs, to keep the blood from clotting

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it before midday, it is disqualified,
because it says 'in the afternoon'.
If he slaughtered it before the daily offering, it is valid,
provided that someone else stirs its blood
until the daily offering's blood is sprinkled.
And if it was sprinkled first, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second section of the same משנה, now dealing with time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before חצות the פסח is פסול. Before the תמיד it is כשר, with stirring of the blood. Even if its blood is thrown first, it is כשר.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines 'not for its eaters' and 'not for its members'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the two terms. 'Not for its eaters' means for a sick or old person. 'Not for its members' means for a different group from the one that signed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What is 'not for its eaters'? Slaughtering it for a sick person or an old person. What is 'not for its registered members'? One group signed up for it, and he slaughtered it for a different group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that explains what the משנה's first two cases actually look like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not its eaters' means people who are unable to eat a כזית of the פסח, like the sick or elderly. 'Not its members' means a group other than the one that signed up for this animal. These are two different problems: one is about being able to eat, the other is about being registered.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
'The Rabbis taught', which introduces a ברייתא
A group registered to eat one פסח

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
What is meant by 'not for its eaters'?
For the sake of a sick person or an old person.
What is meant by 'not for its registered members'?
This group registered for it,
and he slaughtered it for the sake of a different group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the cases in the first section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Not its eaters' means the sick or elderly. 'Not its members' means a different group than the one registered.

steps.title: Where do these rules come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of these rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the פסוקים. This sets up the next move, where it will bring a ברייתא as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not say outright that the wrong eaters make the פסח פסול. So the גמרא wants to know which verse teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these matters?', a request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the cases, the גמרא asks for their Torah source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches that the פסח must be slaughtered for its proper eaters and registered members.

steps.title: The source is the word במכסת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word במכסת that the פסח is slaughtered only for its registered members.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'According to the number of' teaches that the פסח is slaughtered only for those registered for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the word במכסת as a source text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מכסת means a count. Since the Torah says the פסח goes by a count of people, it must be slaughtered for the people already counted on it. This is the source for שלא למנויו being פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to the count', from שמות י״ב:ד
Teaches, used for a lesson drawn from a verse

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'According to the number of' teaches
that the Paschal lamb is slaughtered only for its registered members,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word במכסת teaches that the פסח may be slaughtered only for its registered members. The ברייתא continues next.

steps.title: The repeated verse makes the rule essential
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that slaughtering for unregistered people might be only a missed מצוה while the פסח stays כשר. It rejects this: the Torah says the idea twice (במכסת and תכוסו), and repetition means the rule is לעכב, so the פסח is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that if he slaughtered it for people who are not registered, he only broke a commandment and the offering is still valid. So the verse says 'במכסת' and also 'תכוסו'. The Torah repeated it to show the rule is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks whether breaking the registration rule only breaks a מצוה or actually makes the פסח פסול. It answers that the פסח is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that the פסח is slaughtered for its members, but that alone could be a לכתחילה rule. The ברייתא points out that the Torah says this twice. When the Torah repeats a requirement, the repetition shows it is לעכב, so without it the קרבן fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought'. It introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject.
Breaks a commandment, but the act still counts after the fact.
'The verse teaches'. It brings the Torah source that settles the question.
The verse repeated it.
Essential. Without it, the act is invalid.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'he broke a מצוה but it is כשר' with 'it is פסול'. The whole point of this step is that the פסח is פסול, not just done the wrong way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה in Step 7 can call the פסח פסול, and not just say it was done improperly.

phrases.english: One might think: if he slaughtered it for those not registered for it
phrases.notes: This is the הוה אמינא, the first thought that's about to be rejected.

phrases.english: he would be like one who violated a commandment
but the offering is valid
Therefore the verse says: 'According to the number ... you shall make your count'
phrases.notes: The words מכס and כסס come from the same root, so the verse says the same idea twice.

phrases.english: The verse repeated it to make it essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שְׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָו יְהֵא כְּעוֹבֵר עַל הַמִּצְוָה וְכָשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 11 and turns the source into a rule of פסול.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double wording במכסת and תכוסו shows the registration rule is לעכב, so a פסח slaughtered שלא למנויו is פסול.

steps.title: רבי: תכוסו means 'slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads תכוסו differently. In Aramaic, כוס means 'slaughter', as when someone says 'slaughter this lamb for me'. So the verse ties the slaughter itself to the count of members.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: it is an Aramaic word, like a person who says to his friend, 'Slaughter (כוס) this lamb for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own explanation of the word תכוסו in the verse. He says it means 'slaughter', not 'count'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, במכסת and תכוסו both mean 'counting', and that repetition is what makes the rule לעכב. רבי reads תכוסו as 'slaughter', so the verse says: slaughter it according to the count. This connects the registration directly to the act of שחיטה, showing the registration must be in place when the animal is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.
Aramaic (the Syrian language).
Aramaic for 'slaughter'.
A lamb.

steps.confusionAlert: Here תכוסו does not mean 'count'. For רבי it means 'slaughter'. That is the whole new idea of this step.

phrases.english: Rebbi says:
It is Aramaic,
like a person who says to his friend
'Slaughter this lamb for me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different meaning for the word תכוסו that the ברייתא just used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תכוסו means 'slaughter', so the verse ties the שחיטה of the פסח to its registered count.

steps.title: What is the source for 'not for its eaters'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that it now has a source for שלא למנויו. It asks where the source is for שלא לאוכליו, slaughtering for people who cannot eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for 'not for its registered members'. Where do we learn 'not for its eaters'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It has already covered one of the two cases and now asks for a source for the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (Step 7) and the ברייתא (Step 9) give two separate cases: people who cannot eat (sick or old) and people who are not registered. The verse במכסת only covered registration. So the case of non-eaters still needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We have found' a source for one case.
'From where do we know this?' A request for a source.
For people who cannot eat the פסח.

phrases.english: We have found a source for 'not for its registered members';
from where do we know 'not for its eaters'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָו, שֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case already sourced (members) to the case not yet sourced (eaters).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a פסח slaughtered for people who cannot eat it is פסול.

steps.title: Eaters are linked to registered members
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'איש לפי אכלו תכוסו' puts 'eating' right next to 'counting'. This היקש teaches that eaters share the same law as members, so slaughtering for non-eaters is also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Each man according to his eating, you shall count.' Eaters are compared to registered members.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a verse that mentions eating and counting together. Because they appear together, they get the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verse that teaches the registration rule also mentions 'his eating'. Putting the two side by side is a היקש, a Torah comparison. So just as slaughtering for non-members makes the פסח פסול, slaughtering for non-eaters makes it פסול too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse says'. It introduces the Torah source.
According to his eating.
They are compared (a היקש) because they appear side by side.
The registered members of the group.

steps.whatToRemember: Both disqualifications come from the same verse. Slaughtering for non-members is פסול because of the repeated במכסת/תכוסו. Slaughtering for non-eaters is פסול because 'his eating' is compared (היקש) to 'counting'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the sources for both disqualifications in the משנה of Step 7.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'Each man according to his eating you shall make your count';
eaters are compared to registered members.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש in 'איש לפי אכלו תכוסו' compares eaters to members, so slaughtering שלא לאוכליו is also פסול.
